uncited: GPU-based Voxelization accelerates the conversion of polygon meshes or geometric primitives into discrete volumetric representations by leveraging the massive parallelism of CUDA-capable GPUs [S1, S3].
It solves the performance bottleneck of CPU-based rasterization, enabling real-time voxelization of high-polygon models [S3].

It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by its direct use of CUDA kernels for parallel triangle processing and atomic memory updates, contrasting with CPU parallelization [7135-parallel-cpu-voxelization.md] or specialized structures like linked lists [1187-per-pixel-linked-list-voxelization.md].
An optimized implementation of Schwarz and Seidel's algorithm for surface and solid voxelization [6757-cuda-voxelizer-gpu-voxelization.md].
Uses bit-packed grids and atomic operations; requires watertight meshes for solid mode [6757-cuda-voxelizer-gpu-voxelization.md].
Uses conditional histograms for voxel queries [10393-gpu-based-voxel-query-via-conditional-histogram-computation.md].
The method is based on the algorithm described by Schwarz and Seidel [S1].
It was implemented as a high-performance, real-time solution leveraging CUDA parallelism [S3].
Atomic operations are a key component, though they can introduce contention on older hardware architectures [S1].
